description:
A value whose static evidence has degraded to `any` can silently enter a parameter with a narrower declared type. Struct patterns have a related fallback: when a `defstruct` module has no conventional `@type t`, every field in `struct_assertion_ty` defaults to `any`. Both precision losses are silent today.

## Current repro

```fz
@spec need(integer) :: integer
fn need(x), do: x

fn main() do
  opaque = Kernel.fz_dbg_value(7)
  dbg(need(opaque))
end
```

At origin/main `a3a9761d1209165e5230625b9347cf6b0ad09b83`:

```text
$ fz2 interp --dump activations=/tmp/activations repro.fz
7
7

need/1[any]
  return: any

main/0[]
  ...
  @103-115 => need/1(any) => any
```

The runtime value is valid, but the compiler silently loses the declared `integer` evidence.

The struct-field fallback remains live in `src/compiler2/jobs/semantic.rs::struct_assertion_ty`: a struct with no `@type t` constructs `vec![any; field_names.len()]`.

## Missing diagnostics

Neither `TYPE_PARAM_GRADUATED_TO_ANY` nor `TYPE_STRUCT_FIELD_DEFAULTED_TO_ANY` exists in `src/diag/codes.rs`, and there is no detector in `src/compiler2`.

The warning plumbing already exists: `WarningDiagnosticKey` deduplicates by code, message, and primary span; `ExecutionContext::emit_warning_once` records warnings; source and contract jobs already emit non-fatal warnings through this path.

## Goal

Emit non-fatal, deduplicated warnings when:

1. a parameter with a declared non-`any` contract is analyzed with `any`; or
2. semantic struct-pattern typing must default a field to `any` because the struct has no declared field type.

Explicitly declared `any` must not warn.

## Strategy

1. Add stable diagnostic codes for the two cases.
2. Detect parameter graduation where declared contract evidence and settled activation inputs are both available.
3. Detect field defaulting at the authoritative `struct_assertion_ty` fallback.
4. Emit through the existing warning accumulator.
5. Measure and classify the full library and fixture blast radius before blessing diagnostics; repair genuine precision defects separately rather than suppressing their warnings.

## Checks

- The repro emits exactly one parameter-graduation warning identifying `need/1` parameter 0 and still runs successfully.
- A `defstruct [:x]` pattern without `@type t` emits one field-default warning.
- Adding `@type t :: %Point{x: integer}` removes the field-default warning.
- Declaring a parameter or field as `any` intentionally does not warn.
- Repeated derivations do not duplicate diagnostics.
- Record the current full lib/fixture warning census and keep all existing behavioral tests green.
title: Warn when declared parameters or struct fields silently degrade to any
